models.title: Final-period depreciation to residual value
models.summary: The final period adjusts the declining-balance charge so the remaining book value equals residual value.

relationship.original_equation: Final-period depreciation = beginning book value − residual value
relationship.locator: Double Declining Balance, final-year adjustment and worked truck example
relationship.translation_notes: All quantities are nonnegative monetary amounts; the residual is an estimated terminal book amount.

variables.definition: Remaining carrying value above residual value
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: This is the final period of a policy that allocates all remaining depreciable amount to expense.
Beginning book value and residual value refer to the same asset and currency; beginning book value is no less than residual.
limitations: This branch does not determine whether an ordinary period needs a residual-value cap.
Changes in estimates, impairment, disposal and partial periods require separate treatment.
